####################
## Homework 3     ##
####################

The local, national, and world news have been full of stories about protests in Chicagoland regarding ICE activities, and about complex dynamics between protesters, local governments, federal law enforcement, and the government. In this assignment, I will ask you to use qualitative methods to explore these relationships. The evidence you will use is a collection of news stories from the last three months describing protest activity, government statements, and law enforcement responses in Chicagoland, found on [the class website](https://github.com/jnseawright/ps210/tree/main/Homework/HW3%20Documents).

For this assignment, you are free to work individually or in groups. If you choose
to work collaboratively, please include your name and the names of the people you
worked with on your submitted assignment. You will not be penalized for collaborating.

####################
## Problem 1      ##
####################

Before you start working with the data, please spell out your theory of how Trump's immigration enforcement initiative this fall may have changed the size, scope, and kind of protests that Chicagoland is experiencing. Do your best to spell out the theory with multiple testable implications, in the way that we discussed in class, possibly with a box chart linking steps to show your thinking.

####################
## Problem 2      ##
####################

On the class website, you will find about 22 news stories from the last few months. Look through these and select some that seem relevant. Load them into Taguette and systematically code them, searching for evidence that confirms or defeats your theory as well as other interesting findings. When you are finished, screenshot your list of codes, as well as the summary of tagged text for one of your most interesting codes. 

You should expect to identify at least ten codes, each of which applies to a minimum of two highlights. Your most frequently used codes should probably apply to many more.

####################
## Problem 3      ##
####################

Using the text you highlighted in Problem 2, evaluate which components of your theory from Problem 1 are supported by evidence, which components do not have evidence, and which components perhaps face contradictory evidence. Taken as a whole, does the process-tracing data support, contradict, or simply not decide about your theory? Explain your reasoning.
